findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Assumptions on interest rates may not materialise as planned, and securing cost certainty to Vesting Day is described as a key priority.
findings.detail: The paper lists interest rate assumptions as a key MTFS risk. It describes securing cost certainty to Vesting Day as a priority, which links the borrowing position to the LGR timetable.
findings.matters: A borrowing plan built on rate assumptions that may not hold is a risk that lenders and peer finance officers would test against their own.
findings.figures: No £ figure or rate given in the paper
findings.quote: Assumptions on interest rates may not materialise as planned. Securing cost certainty to Vesting Day is a key priority.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Vacancy margin savings of £400k from staff turnover require active management to be achieved.
findings.detail: The paper lists this as a key MTFS risk. The savings depend on managing turnover actively, rather than on a fixed reduction in establishment.
findings.matters: A savings target that depends on turnover rather than structural change is a specific delivery risk that finance directors at other councils can compare with their own vacancy margins.
findings.figures: £400k annual establishment savings target
findings.quote: Vacancy margin annual establishment savings target requires active management to achieve £400k, from staff turn-over.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: The LGA Corporate Peer Challenge implementation programme is to be closed down as substantially complete in April 2026.
findings.detail: The paper says the Council Delivery Plan required all actions to be completed by March 2026. Internal audit gave the programme arrangements a substantial assurance rating in September 2025.
findings.matters: Closing a peer-review action plan as substantially complete, with an internal audit rating behind it, shows how a council has responded to the peer's financial planning recommendations.
findings.figures: 10 recommendations from June 2024 peer challenge; follow-up visit April 2025
findings.quote: The implementation programme was agreed to be closed down as substantially in April 2026.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: The council has retendered its property valuation contract to Montagu Evans, and says the valuation governance process has been completed.
findings.detail: The paper says the 31 March 2025 property valuation process showed governance and technical issues. The council says it has reviewed and revised the governance process, brought in additional resource, and marked the retendering and governance items as completed.
findings.matters: Valuation weaknesses were one reason the auditors could not gain assurance over property balances, so a finance director at another council facing similar valuation problems would want to see the remedy.
findings.figures: 31st March 2025 (valuation date); no £ figure given in the paper
findings.quote: The Council has retendered the contract for valuation appointing an alternative provider Montagu Evans.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: The Waste collection contract with Serco (circa £5m) has not been extended, and negotiations have not concluded.
findings.detail: The paper says the contract carries significant cost and capital commitment risks. A provision for cost risk is included in the MTFS forecast.
findings.matters: A contract of this value with an unresolved extension, and a provision in the forecast to cover it, is a specific pressure that peer finance officers facing the same contract renewals would compare against their own.
findings.figures: circa £5m (Serco waste collection contract)
findings.quote: The Waste collection contract with Serco (circa £5m) negotiations to extend the contract have not been concluded.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: A contingent repayment of £0.8m on Civic Quarter One Public Estate grant depends on conditions being met by 31 March 2027, and £750k sits on Rushmoor Development Partnership's balance sheet.
findings.detail: The paper says a potential repayment of £0.8m applies if grant conditions are not met by 31st March 2027. It also says the council's £750k share of development agreement costs would be funded from useable revenue reserves if written off.
findings.matters: Contingent grant repayments and written-off development costs both fall on revenue reserves, which is the same reserve base the council is using to balance 2026/27.
findings.figures: £0.8m potential grant repayment; £750k development agreement costs held on RDP balance sheet
findings.quote: with a potential repayment of £0.8m if grant conditions are not met by 31st March 2027.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: An unsecured loan to Farnborough International Limited of £6.482m is due for repayment in tranches over the next three years.
findings.detail: The paper says the financial stability of Farnborough International Limited is reviewed quarterly, to understand its trading and cashflow position and the council's risk.
findings.matters: A large unsecured loan to a council-linked company, repayable in tranches, is a credit exposure a lender or finance director at another council would want to see.
findings.figures: £6.482m unsecured loan; repayment due in tranches in the next three years
findings.quote: There is an unsecured loan to Farnborough International Limited (FIL) of £6.482m due for repayment in tranches in the next three years.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Timing and value of capital receipts are described as a material element of the budgeted reduction in borrowing interest and MRP.
findings.detail: The paper says the council has found it challenging to resource the work needed to deliver capital receipts. Specific oversight of this work's capacity and performance is in place.
findings.matters: Borrowing cost and MRP savings depend on capital receipts arriving on time, so a lender or peer finance officer would want to see whether those receipts are delivered.
findings.figures: No £ figure given in the paper for the budgeted reduction in borrowing interest and MRP
findings.quote: Timing and value of capital receipts are a material element of achieving the budgeted reduction in borrowing interest and MRP

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation for Hampshire and the Solent was withdrawn in September, and the national programme was paused pending review.
findings.detail: The paper says the senior leadership restructure is paused as a result, and the outcome of the review is awaited. The paper's MTFS risk section notes that LGR delay beyond April 2028 would require significant budget savings.
findings.matters: The LGR timetable underpins the council's medium-term financial plan, so a pause changes the assumption that a finance director at another council or a lender would be testing.
findings.figures: April 2028 (LGR delay threshold referenced in the MTFS risks)
findings.quote: the decision relating to Local Government Reorganisation for Hampshire and the Solent was withdrawn

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: The external auditor, EY, says it has a duty to consider whether to raise a public interest report, after expressing continuing concern about financial sustainability and the deficit.
findings.detail: The paper says EY raised the concerns with the Audit and Governance Committee in a members-only pre-meeting on 28 January. It also says EY will keep the council's progress under review.
findings.matters: A public interest report would override the council's democratic control, and a finance director at another council or a lender would want to know when auditors have reached this stage.
findings.figures: 2024/25 Annual Audit report presented 28th January 2026
findings.quote: EY have a duty to consider if it is appropriate to raise a public interest report

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: External auditors issued disclaimed audit opinions on the 2020/21 to 2023/24 accounts, and then a disclaimer on the 2024/25 accounts.
findings.detail: The paper says the auditors could not obtain sufficient evidence over in-year movements, brought-forward balances, and valuations of property, plant and equipment and investment property. Full audit assurance is not expected until the 2026/27 financial statements audit is completed by February 2029.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, can see how far the audit backlog runs and when reserves are expected to be fully assured.
findings.figures: Disclaimed opinions for 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25; full assurance expected by February 2029 (audit deadline)
findings.quote: they issued a disclaimed 2024/25 audit opinion.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: The 2028/29 financial projection is said to require a S114(3) notice if Local Government Reorganisation is delayed beyond 1 April 2028 or the council is not absorbed into a new council on that date.
findings.detail: The S151 officer intends to bring the 2028/29 projection to the new council's attention at the earliest opportunity. The paper says the projection otherwise requires a S114(3) notice on current assumptions. The Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) timetable is therefore the pivot point for the MTFS.
findings.matters: It states a specific year and trigger for a S114(3) notice, which lenders and peer finance officers can weigh against their own councils' LGR timetables.
findings.figures: 1st April 2028 (LGR date); 2028/29 financial projection (no £ figure given in the paper)
findings.quote: the 2028/29 financial projection, which otherwise will, based upon these projections, require a S114(3)

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Rushmoor's S151 officer says the 2026/27 General Fund budget can be balanced with the use of reserves, avoiding a S114(3) notice this financial year.
findings.detail: The paper says the 2026/27 General Fund can be balanced as proposed in the Medium Term Financial Strategy. It adds that the S151 officer must still consider whether the wider MTFS deficit and reserves position requires a S114(3) notice, which it calls much more challenging to assess.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, can see the specific route Rushmoor is using to avoid a S114(3) notice this year: balancing the budget with reserves.
findings.figures: 2026/27 General Fund budget (balanced with use of reserves; no £ figure given in the paper)
findings.quote: the council can balance the 2026/27 General Fund budget, with the use of reserves, avoiding the issuing of a S114(3) in this financial year.

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: Council says there is a strong argument for diversifying funding sources if rates fall below gilt yields plus 0.80%
findings.detail: The paper says the council will evaluate and pursue lower-cost funding alternatives with Arlingclose. It sets the threshold at rates below gilt yields plus 0.80%, and records no forward starting loans arranged in the quarter.
findings.matters: A council signalling it will move away from PWLB and local authority funding toward other sources is relevant to lenders and to peers weighing the same options.
findings.figures: Gilt yields plus 0.80%; no forward starting loans arranged this quarter
findings.quote: There remains a strong argument for diversifying funding sources, particularly if rates can be achieved on alternatives which are below gilt yields + 0.80%.

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: Maturity profile shows 77% of borrowing in the 24 months to 5 years band at 30 September 2026
findings.detail: The paper reports the maturity structure against limits. It shows 14% of borrowing maturing under 12 months, 9% in 12 to 24 months, 77% in 24 months to 5 years, and none beyond 5 years. The paper records compliance with all limits.
findings.matters: A concentration of refinancing in a single period is the exposure a lender and a peer council will want to see when assessing refinancing risk.
findings.figures: 77% in 24 months to 5 years; 14% under 12 months; 9% in 12 to 24 months; 0% beyond 5 years
findings.quote: 24 months and within 5 years 100% 0% 77% Yes

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: Net income from commercial and service investments is budgeted at £7.9m for 2026/27, against £8.9m in 2025/26
findings.detail: The paper shows this income declining across the three years shown, from £8.9m actual in 2025/26 to £7.9m budget in 2026/27 and £7.6m forecast in 2027/28. The proportion of the net revenue stream falls from 67.27% to 44.08% in the budget year, though the paper does not explain the change.
findings.matters: A council whose commercial income is falling as a share of its revenue stream is a comparison point for any peer relying on commercial property income.
findings.quote: The Authority’s income from commercial and service investments as a proportion of its net revenue stream has been and is expected to be as indicated below.

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: £429k of income from strategic pooled funds was received to 30 September 2026, against an £850k budget for 2026/27
findings.detail: The paper says income distributions from strategic pooled funds remained resilient over the period. It also cautions that a six-month figure should not be viewed in isolation, because distribution timing varies by fund.
findings.matters: A finance director relying on pooled fund income to fund revenue budgets will want to see how half-year receipts compare with the annual budget.
findings.figures: £429k received to 30 September 2026; £850k budgeted for 2026/27; £13m invested in strategic pooled funds
findings.quote: Income received up to 30th September was £429k.

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: Council released a £1m reserve held against the statutory override not being extended, in the prior financial year
findings.detail: The paper says the statutory override on pooled fund gains and losses is extended to 1 April 2029 for investments made before 1 April 2024, and not for later investments. It says the council released the £1m reserve it had set aside against the override not being extended, citing current budgetary pressures and the extension.
findings.matters: Other councils holding pooled fund investments will want to know how the override extension is affecting their own reserve decisions.
findings.figures: £1m reserve released
findings.quote: The Authority had set up a reserve of £ 1m to mitigate the impact of the statutory override not being extended.

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: Cash available within three months was £8.4m at 30 September 2026, against a £5m target
findings.detail: The paper reports this liquidity measure as complying with its target. It is the amount of cash available for unexpected payments within a rolling three-month period without new borrowing.
findings.matters: A council's three-month liquidity headroom is a standard measure that lenders and finance directors compare across councils.
findings.figures: £8.4m actual; £5m target
findings.quote: Total cash available within 3 months £8.4m £5m Yes

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: The average rate on £15m of short-term loans was 4.23% at 30 September 2026, against 4.90% on £32m three months earlier
findings.detail: The paper reports that the council's short-term loan average fell over the quarter, even though market rates for short-term local authority borrowing rose over the period. The figures cover different loan balances at each date.
findings.matters: A fall in the average rate on short-term loans against a rising market is a result a peer council would want to understand how to replicate.
findings.figures: 4.23% on £15m at 30.09.26; 4.90% on £32m three months earlier
findings.quote: The average rate on the Council’s short-term loans at 30th September 2026 on £15m was 4.23%, this compares with 4.90% on £32m 3 months ago.

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: Short-term borrowing from other local authorities cost 3.8% to 5.5% over the period, above Bank Rate of 3.75%
findings.detail: The paper says the cost of short-term local authority borrowing rose throughout the period. It attributes this to many authorities relying more on the short-term market and to low cash levels and non-receipt of SEND grants.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders in the local authority market will want to see how short-term cash costs are moving across the sector.
findings.figures: 3.8% to 5.5%; Bank Rate 3.75%
findings.quote: The cost of short-term borrowing from other local authorities has been above Bank Rate during the period at 3.8% to 5.5%

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: The paper says borrowing rates have started to rise above the 4.5% MTFS assumption
findings.detail: The council's strategy was to move toward longer-term borrowing for cost certainty, but the paper says rates have recently risen above the assumption in the medium-term financial strategy. It says the council is taking regular advice from Arlingclose to minimise costs.
findings.matters: A council whose budget assumes 4.5% borrowing costs and sees rates above that will face the same question about its financing budget.
findings.figures: MTFS assumption rate 4.5%
findings.quote: recently rates have started to rise above our MTFS assumption rate of 4.5%.

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: The PWLB 20-year certainty rate rose from 6.13% to 6.61% in the six months to 30 September 2026
findings.detail: The paper gives the 10-year PWLB certainty rate as 5.62% at the start of the period and 6.17% at the end. The rate table in the same appendix shows the 20-year rate at 6.15% on 1 April 2026, which differs from the 6.13% in the text.
findings.matters: Long-dated PWLB rates rising well above a 4.5% planning assumption changes the cost of replacing maturing debt for every council borrowing over these periods.
findings.quote: Rates for 20-year maturity loans moved from 6.13% to 6.61% during the period

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: Council holds £132m of commercial property investments and will review exit options before further additional borrowing
findings.detail: The paper says most of the £132m of commercial property was bought primarily for financial return, before the change in the CIPFA Prudential Code. It also says the Authority has no new plans to borrow to invest primarily for financial return.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council holding yield-driven property will want to compare this exit review with their own options.
findings.figures: £132m commercial property; £138.8m total non-treasury investments
findings.quote: Before undertaking further additional borrowing the Council will review the options for exiting these investments.

findings.paper_title: Item 6. Treasury Management and Non-Treasury Management
findings.headline: Council held £110m of loans at 30 September 2026, a decrease of £39m on 31 March 2026
findings.detail: The paper reports external borrowing falling from £149.0m at 31 March 2026 to £110m at 30 September 2026, with the short-term PWLB balance of £62.0m shown as nil at the later date. The forecast for 31 March 2027 is £95.0m.
findings.matters: A council reducing its external debt by about a quarter in six months is a change a lender and a peer finance team would both want to see the cause of.
findings.quote: At 30th September 2026 the Council held £110m of loans, (a decrease of £39m on 31st March 2026)

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: Corporate risk register lists 'Lack of deliverable / viable masterplan proposal in current economic context' as a regeneration risk with residual score 12 (High), with a Strategic Delivery Review of the masterplan underway
findings.detail: The register records high public and political interest in the scheme and a masterplan that is not yet deliverable or viable in the current economic context. Mitigations include the Strategic Delivery Review, exploring disposal of land interests to Homes England or other parties, and a regeneration fund now on Plot D.
findings.matters: A capital scheme whose masterplan is not yet viable, with the council exploring disposal and external funding, is a position a lender and a peer finance director would weigh against their own regeneration exposure.
findings.figures: Residual risk score 12 (High); OPE funding of £1.75m secured for early enabling works
findings.quote: Lack of deliverable / viable masterplan proposal in current economic context.

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: Corporate risk register records the property portfolio income risk with residual score 9 (High) and target 6 (Medium), with the portfolio now asset-managed by LSH Investment Management
findings.detail: The register describes significant loss of income from the property portfolio, driven by deteriorating economic conditions, property market downturn and changing consumer or business habits. Mitigations include the appointment of LSHIM to asset manage the entire investment portfolio and a new investment portfolio manager role.
findings.matters: Commercial property income is a revenue source that lenders and finance directors at other councils track closely, and the register links it to rent-free periods and lettings.
findings.figures: Residual risk score 9 (High); target risk score 6 (Medium)
findings.quote: Significant loss of income from the Council’s property portfolio arising from a variety of reasons including deteriorating economic conditions, downturn in the property market and changing consumer or business habits.

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: Corporate risk register's 'Inaccurate reporting of financial position' has a residual score of 12 (High) with an upward trend, and SLT began challenging monthly variances from August 2026
findings.detail: The register says budget management is now completed monthly by services with service accountants, and that a new budget management finance system module has been implemented. A 'No PO, No pay process' has been in place from 1 April 2026, and SLT now reviews the monthly financial position and challenges variances.
findings.matters: Monthly budget monitoring with challenge from SLT, and a new PO process, are controls that a finance director elsewhere would compare against their own forecasting and variance processes.
findings.figures: Residual risk score 12 (High), trend upward; target risk score 4 (Medium); 'No PO, No pay' from 1 April 2026
findings.quote: SLT now review the monthly financial position and challenge variances starting in August 2026

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: Corporate risk register records a new finance capacity risk, 'Finance unable to adequately discharge responsibilities, lack of suitably qualified or experienced staff', with residual score 6 (Medium), and reliance on interim resources for year-end accounts
findings.detail: The register lists demands for finance support greater than available staff time, and audit opinion risk if staff are not available or suitably qualified. Mitigations include reliance on interim resources to lead technical year-end accounting and production of the Statement of Accounts, plus outsourcing of Collection Fund accounting and treasury management support.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council will recognise the reliance on interim year-end resource and outsourced Collection Fund and treasury work as a capacity pressure that affects the accounts and audit timetable.
findings.figures: Residual risk score 6 (Medium), trend N/A
findings.quote: Demands for finance support are greater than available staff time leading to poor decision making

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: SIAP's March 2026 internal audit of risk management gives overall assurance of 'Reasonable', with 3 medium-priority findings and no high-priority findings
findings.detail: The audit's findings cover archived risks lacking a recorded basis for closure, the Audit and Governance Committee not receiving the risk register at the frequency the policy requires, and risk not being a documented standing item at service meetings. The paper says all other actions from the audit are complete.
findings.matters: The assurance grade and the three medium findings give a peer finance officer a benchmark for the risk management control environment, and the committee-reporting finding shows the same gap that other councils have reported.
findings.figures: Priority 1 (high): 0; Priority 2 (medium): 3; Priority 3 (low): 0
findings.quote: Reasonable: There is a generally sound system of governance, risk management and control in place.

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: Council asks Audit and Governance Committee to extend risk management audit action 1.1 from 30 September 2026 to 31 March 2027, citing IT team resource
findings.detail: The action concerns updating the service risk register format to record narrative for archived risks. The paper says all other actions from the March 2026 SIAP audit are complete, and that the Corporate Risk Manager is monitoring archived risks manually in the meantime.
findings.matters: An internal audit action slipping its deadline, with resource cited as the reason, is the kind of audit follow-up a finance director or peer council would compare against their own action tracking.
findings.figures: Deadline moved from 30.09.2026 to 31.03.2027; the SIAP audit contains 3 medium-priority findings and 0 high-priority findings
findings.quote: The Council has been unable to complete this action due to resource issues within the IT team who provide the formal expertise to carry out the updates to the system.

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: Financial Statements audit risk ('unqualified audit opinion is delayed') is recorded with residual score 6 (Medium), and the register states 'Improved position on 25/26 accounts, back on track for fully qualified accounts'
findings.detail: The register says the return to an unqualified audit opinion by 2027/28 has been delayed by lack of progress on PPE valuations, reserves and disclosures. Mitigations listed include new valuers procured and an improved working relationship with the external auditors, EY.
findings.matters: A council returning to a fully qualified set of accounts after an audit problem is a point a finance director or lender tracks, and the register ties it to valuations and reserves.
findings.figures: Residual risk score 6 (Medium); target to return to an unqualified audit opinion by 2027/28
findings.quote: Improved position on 25/26 accounts, back on track for fully qualified accounts. Continuing to work with auditors.

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: Corporate risk register records the external borrowing risk (interest rate and refinancing, residual score 12 High) as 'No longer a risk - it is now being managed by SLT as a live issue/incident'
findings.detail: The register lists the risk as new, with a target score of 4 (Medium). It notes the target is likely to remain high given current borrowing level and forecasts, and describes a planned move to both longer-term and short-term borrowing, plus asset disposals to reduce long-term borrowing need.
findings.matters: Lenders and finance directors will want to see that a council has moved borrowing from a monitored risk to an active SLT issue, and that the target score is not expected to be reached.
findings.figures: Residual risk score 12 (High); target risk score 4 (Medium); largest risk gap of -8 in the 05/11/2026 risk report
findings.quote: No longer a risk - it is now being managed by SLT as a live issue/incident.

findings.paper_title: Item 5. Risk Management Process Annual Update
findings.headline: Corporate risk register's new strategic risk 'MTFS is not financially sustainable' has a residual score of 16 (High) and a target of 4 (Medium), with the deficit options to be identified in November 2026
findings.detail: The register says the MTFS shows the revenue deficit exceeding reserves available for a statutory legal budget from 2028/29 onwards. Cabinet and SLT are to identify options to rectify the deficit in November 2026, and these depend partly on the government pause on LGR.
findings.matters: A finance director here or at another council will want to see how a deficit-to-reserves gap is being scored and when remedial options are due, since this is a stated position rather than a closed deficit.
findings.figures: Residual risk score 16 (High); target risk score 4 (Medium); deficit exceeds reserves from 2028/29 onwards; largest risk gap of -12 in the 05/11/2026 risk report
findings.quote: MTFS 2026/27 indicates the level of revenue deficit exceeds the level of reserves available to set a statutory legal budget in 2028/29 onwards.

findings.paper_title: Draft Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Bank, payroll and billing reconciliations are prepared, but review sign-off is not recorded.
findings.detail: The auditor reports that these reconciliations are prepared, but there is no signed evidence that they have been reviewed. This is listed among the control observations with improvement recommendations.
findings.matters: Unrecorded reconciliation review is a control gap that finance directors at other councils can check in their own close processes.
findings.quote: Bank, payroll and billing reconciliations are prepared, but review sign-off is not recorded.

findings.paper_title: Draft Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Management corrected all misstatements above the £102,000 reporting threshold, and the auditor reports no uncorrected misstatements.
findings.detail: The corrected items include reclassification of debtors and creditors of £1.17 million, revaluation of surplus assets of £1.77 million and an overstatement of Assets Held for Sale of £790,000. The auditor also reports that there are no uncorrected misstatements.
findings.matters: The volume and size of draft-stage errors show how far the draft accounts needed correcting before audit, which is a benchmark other councils can compare against.
findings.quote: Management have corrected all misstatements above our reporting threshold of £102,000.

findings.paper_title: Draft Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: The Annual Governance Statement was not published on 30 June 2026, the date required by the Accounts and Audit Regulations 2015.
findings.detail: The paper states that the financial statements were published by the 30 June 2026 deadline, but the Annual Governance Statement was not. The AGS also did not include a final Internal Audit opinion.
findings.matters: Councils will compare their own AGS publication timing and Head of Internal Audit opinion inclusion against the statutory deadline.
findings.figures: 30 June 2026
findings.quote: The Annual Governance Statement was not published on 30 June 2026, as required by the Accounts and Audit Regulations 2015.

findings.paper_title: Draft Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: The auditor was able to provide assurance on property, plant and equipment, investment property and capital grants received in advance in 2025/26.
findings.detail: The paper states that significant progress has been made in rebuilding assurance following the 2023/24 disclaimed opinion. It says all planned procedures were completed in 2025/26, and the auditor describes the expected return to an unqualified opinion as possible by 2027/28.
findings.matters: Councils that received disclaimed opinions across the sector will be watching how quickly assurance can be rebuilt on individual balance sheet areas.
findings.figures: 2023/24 disclaimed opinion; 2027/28
findings.quote: Significant progress has been made in rebuilding assurance following the 2023/24 disclaimed opinion.

findings.paper_title: Draft Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: The auditor expects to issue a qualified opinion on the 2025/26 statement of accounts, with an unqualified opinion possibly by 2027/28.
findings.detail: The paper says the auditor has substantially completed the audit and, subject to outstanding procedures and review, expects to issue a qualified opinion. It also states that an unqualified opinion may be possible by 2027/28, on the MHCLG audit recovery trajectory.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another council following the national backlog recovery will want to see how the same recovery timetable applies to their own accounts.
findings.quote: we expect to issue a qualified opinion.

findings.paper_title: Draft Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Revenue savings were achieved in 2025/26, but recurrent savings sufficient to balance future budgets have not yet been identified.
findings.detail: The paper records that revenue savings were achieved in 2025/26. It also states that the Council has not yet identified and delivered sufficient recurrent savings to balance future budgets, and that a planned £0.5 million permanent base budget reduction is part of the Financial Resilience Plan.
findings.matters: The gap between one-off savings delivered and recurrent savings still needed is the central test of whether a council can close a multi-year deficit without drawing on reserves.
findings.figures: £0.5 million each year for the four years commencing 2025/26
